pr_title: [Authentication] Use existing principal for single scheme

issue_context.title: Windows authorization fails when specifying both Roles and AuthenticationSchemes
issue_context.body:

### Describe the bug
When using Windows authentication (using the Negotiate package), specifying both `Roles` and `AuthenticationSchemes` in the `[Authorize]` attribute fails when it should succeed.

It's likely to be caused by the `PolicyEvaluator`, which merges identities into a single principal, see [here](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v5.0.5/src/Security/Authorization/Policy/src/PolicyEvaluator.cs#L46). However this means the `WindowsPrincipal` is lost which is crucial to decoding the `groupsid` groups from AD when the authorization calls `IsInRole`.

Is this expected behavior? Am I doing something wrong?

### To Reproduce
<!--
We ❤ code! Point us to a minimalistic repro project hosted in a GitHub repo.
For a repro project, create a new ASP.NET Core project using the template of your your choice, apply the minimum required code to result in the issue you're observing.

We will close this issue if:
- the repro project you share with us is complex. We can't investigate custom projects, so don't point us to such, please.
- if we will not be able to repro the behavior you're reporting
-->

Controller endpoint:
```c#
[ApiController]
public class WeatherForecastController : ControllerBase
{
    [Authorize(Roles = "Everyone", AuthenticationSchemes = NegotiateDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)]
    [HttpGet("weatherforecast")]
    public IActionResult Get()
    {
        // This endpoint call fails

        // Type of user is `ClaimsPrincipal`
        // If I remove `AuthenticaitonSchemes`, it is `WindowsPrincipal`
        var user = User;

        return Ok();
    }
}
```

Vanilla startup using Kestrel:
```c#
public void ConfigureServices(IServiceCollection services)
{
    services.AddControllers();

    services
        .AddAuthentication(NegotiateDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)
        .AddNegotiate();
}

public void Configure(IApplicationBuilder app, IWebHostEnvironment env)
{
    app
        .UseRouting()
        .UseAuthentication()
        .UseAuthorization()
        .UseEndpoints(endpoints =>
        {
            endpoints.MapControllers();
        });
}
```

### Exceptions (if any)
<!-- 
Include the exception you get when facing this issue
-->

### Further technical details
- ASP.NET Core version `5.0`
- Include the output of `dotnet --info`
- The IDE (VS / VS Code/ VS4Mac) you're running on, and its version
comments: Is there a reason you need to specify the auth scheme on Authorize? You've already set it as the default scheme in startup.

This was simply to illustrate the problem.  

In reality, we are using both Negotiate and JWT, neither of which are set as defaults. Then we set the default policy in 'UseAuthorization' to accept both schemes. This approach works flawlessly, except for the scenario I described above, where an AD role will fail to authorize since the WindowsPrincipal is stripped away from the resulting 'User' principal object.

Just checking. I agree this is problematic behavior. It's not clear why MergeUserPrincipal is even creating a new principal when there's only one scheme. If it no-op'd the first time then this would work in the general case.  We could also have it sniff for WindowsPrincipals coming in and re-create that.

As for mitigations, it looks like you can replace the IPolicyEvaluator service with your own copy that does as you like.

Yeah that's what we've done, but I'm sure this issue will bite someone down the line, so would be good to either have the behaviour described in docs or have a bug fix for it. I'm happy to take a stab at a PR if you'd like.
@HaoK thoughts on fixing this via no-oping or type sniffing?
I think its reasonable to skip doing anything when only a single scheme to the principal if only a single scheme is specified if that will fix this problem
@robertcoltheart want to give it a try?

Thanks for contacting us.
